spans.s:
bādhita
(‘contradicted’)
------------------------------------------
In the न्याय school of Indian philo-sophy, a material fallacy is technically called ‘hetvābhāsa,’ which literally means that a हेतु or reason which appears as, but really is not, a valid reason. Out of the five hetvābhāsas generally listed, ‘bādhita’ is the last.
Consider the sentence agniranuṣṇaḥ dravyatvāt, ‘Fire is cold, since it is a substance’. Here anuṣṇatva or coldness is the साध्य (major term) and द्रव्य or substance is the हेतु (middle term). The non-existence of coldness, nay more, the existence of hotness, is perceived in fire by our sense of touch. So, we have to reject हेतु or the middle term, dravyatva (being a substance), as it is बाधित or contradicted by another means of knowledge (here, प्रत्यक्ष or direct perception).

bādha
(‘that which contradicts’)
------------------------------------------
The word has several meanings: अभाव or absence; pratibandha or obstacle; pīḍā or harassment. However, it is the न्याय school (of इन्दिअन् फिलोसोफ्य्) that uses it as a technical term of लोगिच्.
In the sentence, parvato vahnimān dhūmāt (‘The hill is fiery, since there is smoke there’), vahni or fire is called ‘sādhya’ (the major term), parvata or hill is called ‘pakṣa’ (the minor term) and dhūma or smoke as ‘hetu’ or ‘liṅga’ (the middle term).
In a situation where the साध्य does not exist in the पक्ष, then the पक्ष is called बाध. For instance, in the sentence hrado vahnimān dhūmāt (‘The lake is fiery, since there is smoke there’) the minor term hrada or lake, which is the पक्ष, is ‘bādha’ since it is impossible for the fire, the साध्य, to exist in the lake. The lake obstructs or prevents (bādha = obstacle) fire from existing in it.
Many more varieties of बाध are discussed in the works of Indian लोगिच्.
